Company KW is being sold, and both Company A and Company B were considering the purchase. The price of Company KW is some percentage more than Company A has in assets, and this same price is also 100% more than Company B has in assets. If Companies A and B were to merge and combine their assets, the price of Company KW would be approximately 85.71428571428571% of these combined assets. What is the percentage by which the price of Company KW is more than Company A's assets?

John works at 3 different hospitals. At the first hospital, he sees 20 different patients each day. At the second hospital, he sees 20% more individual patients a day than at the first hospital. At the third hospital, he sees 15% more individual patients a day than at the first hospital. He works 5 days a week for 50 weeks a year, but he also takes 2 weeks of vacation during which he does not work. How many patients does he treat in a year, considering the vacation weeks?

Company KW is being sold, and both Company A and Company B were considering the purchase. The price of Company KW is 30% more than Company A has in assets, and this same price is also some percentage more than Company B has in assets. If Companies A and B were to merge and combine their assets, the price of Company KW would be approximately 78.78787878787878% of these combined assets. What is the percentage by which the price of Company KW is more than Company B's assets?

Maximoff's monthly bill is $60. After he started working from home, his expenses increased as follows: his electricity bill increased by forty-five percent, his internet bill increased by thirty percent, and he added a $25 subscription for a faster internet connection. Furthermore, he needed to pay $15 for a cloud storage subscription and started to rent a virtual desktop solution for $35 per month. The total cost of his monthly bill considering all these factors will be?

Nancy takes 4 antacids per day when she eats Thai food, 3 antacids per day when she eats Indian food, 2 antacids per day when she eats Mexican food, 1 antacid per day when she eats Italian food, and no antacid on days she eats other cuisines. If Nancy eats Thai twice a week, Indian three times a week, Mexican twice a week, and Italian once a week, how many antacids does she take per month, considering a month has 30 days and she follows her eating schedule consistently?

Last year, Springtown Hardware ordered 3 claw hammers and 2 ball-peen hammers in June, 4 claw hammers and 3 ball-peen hammers in July, 6 claw hammers and 7 ball-peen hammers in August, and 9 claw hammers and 11 ball-peen hammers in September. If the pattern continues for each type of hammer separately and there is a 5% increase in the combined orders due to seasonal demand in October, how many hammers will the store order in total in October (considering both types)?

The taxi fare standard in Wenzhou is as follows: the starting price is 10 yuan (i.e., a fare of 10 yuan is charged for a distance of up to 4 kilometers), and for every additional kilometer beyond 4 kilometers, an extra 1.5 yuan is charged (distances less than 1 kilometer are rounded up to 1 kilometer). If someone travels from point A to point B and the fare is 19 yuan, calculate the maximum distance traveled in kilometers, considering the rounding rule for distances.

Mary is going on a business trip. It takes 10 minutes for her Uber to get to her house and 5 times longer to get to the airport. It takes 15 minutes to check her bag and some time to get through security. Then she has to wait for 20 minutes for her flight to start boarding and twice as long before the plane is ready to take off. This process will take 3 hours total. What is the ratio of the time it takes to get through security to the time it takes to check her bag?

Cloud 9 Diving Company has taken individual bookings worth $12,000 and group bookings worth $16,000. The group bookings came with a 10% discount on the total price. However, due to last-minute cancellations, the company had to return refunds of varying amounts: $500 for 3 individual bookings, $300 for 2 individual bookings, and a total of $800 for 2 group bookings. Calculate the total amount of money the company has taken after considering the refunds and discounts.

Sharmila works two jobs. At her first job, she works 10 hours per day on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, and 8 hours per day on Tuesday and Thursday. She earns $15 per hour at this job, and receives a bonus of $20 per day on the days she works 10 hours. At her second job, she works 5 hours on Saturday and earns $12 per hour, with an additional $10 bonus on that day. How much does Sharmila earn in dollars per hour on average, considering both jobs and bonus payments?

Upon receiving the $4000 stimulus check instead of $2000, Mr. Eithan decided to share the amount among his larger family. He gave 1/4 of the amount to his wife, 3/8 of the remaining amount to his first son, 25% of the remaining amount to his second son, and $500 to his third son. Additionally, he gave 15% of the remaining amount to his daughter, and kept the rest in their family's savings account. Calculate the total amount he kept in the family's savings account.

Axel bought an aquarium that was marked down 50% from an original price of $120. He also used a 10% off coupon on the marked down price. In addition to the aquarium, he bought aquatic plants, decorations, and fish food which cost a total of $75 before tax. The sales tax for the aquarium was 5% whereas the sales tax for the other items was 8%. What was the total cost Axel paid for the aquarium and the additional items, considering the discount and sales tax rates?

Consider three stocks A, B, and C with the following information:

Stock A has a face value of $1,000, a market price of $1,200, and a yield of 18%.

Stock B has a face value of $1,000, a market price of $800, and a yield of 22%.

Stock C has a face value of $1,000, a market price of $1,000, and a yield of 15%.

Suppose an investor holds $5,000 in Stock A, $3,000 in Stock B, and $2,000 in Stock C. Calculate the weighted average yield for the investor's portfolio.

In a candy store, there are three types of candies for sale: caramel candies for 3 rubles, toffees for 5 rubles, and chocolates for 10 rubles. Varja wanted to buy exactly 8 candies of each type and brought 200 rubles with her. In the morning, she saw announcements in the store: "When you buy three chocolates, you get a free toffee at the checkout." and "When you buy three toffees, you get a free caramel candy at the checkout." How much money will Varja have left?

Tony tries to drink more water, so he has been tracking how much water he drinks. Yesterday, he drank 48 ounces of water, which is 4% less than what he drank the day before. On the day before yesterday, Tony drank 5% more water than he did two days ago. Additionally, Tony consumed 10% of his daily water intake from sources like fruits, soup, and other drinks two days ago. Considering only the water he drank directly, how much water did Tony drink two days ago?

John's household has 3 toilets with different water usages per flush: the first one uses 5 gallons, the second one uses 3.5 gallons, and the third one uses 6 gallons. On average, each toilet gets flushed 10 times per day for the first toilet, 7 times for the second toilet, and 12 times for the third toilet. John replaces all three toilets with new ones that use 80% less water per flush. Calculate how much water John saved in June, considering June has 30 days.

To address the difficulty residents face in accessing medical care, the municipal government decided to reduce the price of medications. After two price reductions, the price per box of a certain medication is 100 yuan, which is 19% lower than the original price. However, the price is still considered high, so a third price reduction is decided. If the percentage of each price reduction is the same, how much will each box cost after the third price reduction?

Joe and Adam initially built a garden wall with five courses of bricks. They then realized the wall was too low, so they added seven more courses. If each course originally had 450 bricks, and they took out 1/3 of the bricks in the first added course, 1/4 in the second, 1/5 in the third, 1/6 in the fourth, 1/7 in the fifth, 1/9 in the sixth and only 10 bricks in the last course for easy checkup of the garden, calculate the total number of bricks the wall has.

Company KW is being sold, and both Company A and Company B were considering the purchase. The price of Company KW is 20% more than Company A has in assets, and this same price is also some percentage more than Company B has in assets. If Companies A and B were to merge and combine their assets, the price of Company KW would be approximately 75% of these combined assets. What is the percentage by which the price of Company KW is more than Company B's assets?

Redo's manufacturing costs for sets of horseshoes include a $10,000 initial outlay, $20 per set for the first 300 sets, and $15 per set for each set beyond the first 300. They can sell the sets at $50 each for the first 400 sets, and then $45 for each additional set. If profit is revenue from sales minus manufacturing costs, and the company produces and sells 800 sets of horseshoes, what was their profit considering the variable costs and price discounts?

Last year, Manfred received 26 paychecks. Each of his first 6 paychecks was $750, and each of his remaining paychecks was $20 more than each of his first 6 paychecks. Additionally, Manfred had a bonus of $250 added to his 10th paycheck and a medical deductible of $120 taken from his 20th paycheck. To the nearest dollar, what was the average (arithmetic mean) amount of his paychecks for the year, taking into account his bonus and the medical deductible?

Alfred buys an old scooter for $4700 and spends 10% of the purchase price on initial repairs. After a few months, he invests another $500 on maintenance, and an additional 5% of the total repair costs on safety upgrades. When he sells the scooter, there is a 12% sales tax on the selling price. If he sells the scooter for $5800 (before tax), calculate his profit/gain as a percentage after considering all the expenses and tax on the final selling price.

During a physics class, the teacher brought out a 1-meter long wire, which has a break somewhere that prevents it from conducting electricity (this break is not visible from the outside). How can you quickly locate the fault? It would be quite troublesome to check the wire segment by segment. Think about it, what is the most reasonable way to work? To narrow down the location of the break to about 3-4 centimeters, how many times do you need to check?

John plays paintball 3 times a month. Each time he plays he buys 3 boxes of paintballs. They cost $25 per box. Additionally, he spends $40 per month on equipment maintenance and $10 on travel costs to the paintball field each time he goes. If he buys 12 or more boxes of paintballs in a month, he receives a discount of 15% on paintball costs. Considering all these factors, how much does John spend in total, including discounts, on paintball per month?

the distance from city a to city b is 180 miles. while driving from city a to city b, bob drives at a constant speed of 40 miles per hour. alice leaves city a 30 minutes after bob. during alice's journey, she encounters adverse weather conditions which reduce her average speed by 15%. what is the minimum constant speed in miles per hour that alice must exceed in order to arrive in city b before bob, considering the impact of the weather conditions?

You have a patchwork quilt that two young ladies sewed together for charity. When they started sewing two pieces, each made by them separately, into one, it turned out that the shape and size of these pieces were exactly the same. The challenge is to find out where exactly the pieces of the quilt are joined.

Can you undo the quilt at the seam into two parts of the same shape and size? It might seem like a matter of a few minutes, but... let's see!

Jacob's water tank can hold up to 350 liters of water. Jacob collects water from the river and rain to fill his water tank. The daily water collection varies based on weather conditions and river flow. On average, he can collect 300 to 600 milliliters of water from the rain and 900 to 1500 milliliters of water from the river every day. How many days does Jacob need to fill up his water tank, considering the variable rate of daily water collection?

Lisa, Kay, and Ben were asked by their mother to clean their room. Lisa can clean the room in 8 hours, Kay in 12 hours, and their younger brother Ben takes 16 hours to clean the room. Additionally, their cousin, Sarah, can clean the room in 24 hours if she helps them. Also, Lisa must also pause for 2 breaks of 15 minutes each during the cleaning process. How long will it take if they all clean their room together without considering Lisa's break?

Hortense loves daisies, sunflowers, and tulips. She planted 25 daisy seeds, 25 sunflower seeds, and 30 tulip seeds in her flower bed. If 60% of the daisy seeds germinate, 80% of the sunflower seeds germinate, and 70% of the tulip seeds germinate, and 80% of the resulting plants produce flowers, what will be the total number of plants that produce flowers? Additionally, consider that 10% of the germinated plants die before producing any flowers.

Calculate the number of moles of calcium carbonate formed when 3 moles of calcium hydroxide, 3 moles of carbon dioxide, and 2 moles of sulfuric acid react. The primary reaction is between calcium hydroxide and carbon dioxide, while the side reaction is between calcium hydroxide and sulfuric acid. Consider that these reactions proceed to completion:

Primary reaction: 
Ca(OH)2 + CO2 -> CaCO3 + H2O

Side reaction:
Ca(OH)2 + H2SO4 -> CaSO4 + 2 H2O

Calculate the speed of a boat in still water (in km/hr), if in one hour, the boat goes at varying speeds downstream due to water current and wind resistance, and at 4 km/hr upstream. The water current varies between 2-4 km/hr, and the wind resistance affects the speed by -1 to +1 km/hr throughout the downstream journey. Take into consideration the combined effect of water current and wind resistance to determine the boat's speed in still water.

Tammy wants to run a total of 3500 meters per week, but on weekdays, she runs 10% more and on weekends, she runs 20% less than her average distance per day. If her school track is 50 meters around, and a nearby public track is 100 meters around, she runs on the school track during weekdays and on weekends she goes to the public track. Considering Sunday as a rest day, how many loops should she make on each track per day from Monday to Saturday?

1500 men have provisions for 17 days, with each man consuming 2 kg of food per day. However, after 10 days, 280 men with high metabolisms join the group, and each of them consumes 3 kg of food per day. In addition to that, 40 men who are on a special diet join the group, and each of them consumes only 1 kg food per day. For how many days will the provisions last now, considering the increased food consumption rates for different groups of men?

Bruce's aunt gave him $71 to spend on clothes at the mall. He bought 5 shirts that cost $5 each, a pair of pants that cost $26, 2 pairs of socks for $3 each, and a belt. The original price of the belt is $12, but it has a 25% discount. Additionally, Bruce has a voucher that grants him a 10% discount on his total purchase. How much money does Bruce have left to buy more clothes after using the voucher and considering the discounts on the belt?

Molly will be sending Christmas gifts to the following relatives:
- 2 parents
- 4 brothers
- 1 sister
- 4 brothers' spouses
- 12 children of brothers (4 brothers * 3 children each)
- 1 sister's spouse
- 2 children of sister
- 2 grandparents
- 3 cousins

If she sends one package to each of these relatives by mail, considering the cost of $7 per package, how much will Molly spend on sending all of the gifts by mail to her relatives, in dollars?

For the main course, four teams were asked to prepare 500 pieces of fish fillets within a deadline of 3 hours. The first team completed 189 pieces in 1 hour, and the second team completed 131 pieces in 1.5 hours. The third team has a production rate of 45 fish fillets per hour. Considering the remaining time left and the additional fish fillets needed, calculate the required increased production rate for the fourth team to meet the deadline.

A student scored an average of 75 marks across 5 subjects: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Computer Science. The average of the student's marks in Physics, Mathematics, and Biology is 85. The student scored an average of 70 in Physics, Chemistry, and Computer Science. Considering that Physics carries a weightage of 20%, Chemistry 25%, Mathematics 20%, Biology 15%, and Computer Science 20%, what are the marks obtained in Physics?

A particular store purchased a stock of turtleneck sweaters and marked up its cost by 20%. During the New Year season, it further marked up its prices by 25% of the original retail price. In February, the store then offered a discount of 8%. Additionally, the store faces fluctuating shipping costs, which adds an extra 5% on average to the stocking price. Considering these factors, what was the store's profit on the items sold in February?

Miranda is stuffing feather pillows using a mix of goose and duck feathers. She needs two pounds of feathers for each pillow. A pound of goose feathers is approximately 300 feathers, while a pound of duck feathers is approximately 500 feathers. Her goose has approximately 3600 feathers and her duck has approximately 4000 feathers. How many pillows can she stuff after she plucks both the goose and the duck, considering the mix of feathers?

A motorboat takes 4 hours to travel 24 miles down a river with the help of a constant river's current and a steady headwind. On the return trip upstream, it takes the motorboat 6 hours to cover the same distance, however, this time experiencing a change in wind direction to a tailwind. If we consider the river's current speed as 'c', the headwind speed as 'h', and the tailwind speed as 't', calculate the rate of the current in the river.

I went to the music shop and saw CDs of The Life Journey for $100, A Day a Life for $50, and When You Rescind for $85 on display. The shop was offering a 20% discount on The Life Journey and a buy one get one free offer for A Day a Life. I decided to buy 3 CDs of The Life Journey, 4 CDs of A Day a Life (considering the offer), and 2 CDs of When You Rescind to share with my friends. What is the total amount of money I spent in the shop?

Jack has six plates with a flower pattern, nine plates with a checked pattern, and three plates with a striped pattern. He buys new squared-number-of-checked-plates polka dotted plates and 4/9 of the original number of checked plates with wave patterns. Afterward, he smashes 10% of the flowered plates, 15% of the checked plates, and 20% of the striped plates, rounding down to the nearest whole number. How many plates does he have left?

Chris went shopping during a sale and bought 5 DVD movies at a 20% discount, 8 Blu-ray movies at their regular price, and 3 4K Ultra HD movies at a special offer. The usual prices for movies are $15 for DVDs, $20 for Blu-rays, and $25 for 4K Ultra HDs. There is also a 10% sales tax that gets added to the final cost of the movies. What is the average price Chris paid per movie after considering the discounts, special offers, and taxes?

Nathan plays amateur baseball. He played for 3 hours for two weeks, every day. His friend Tobias played for 5 hours every day, but only for one week. Another friend, Leo played for 2.5 hours for 10 days, while their coach Maddison was present 6 hours a day but only on weekdays for three weeks. Considering 1 week as 7 days, calculate the total number of hours Nathan, Tobias, Leo and Maddison have spent playing or being at the ballpark.

The new individual income tax law has been implemented since January 1, 2019. According to the "Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China," it is known that the part of the actual wages and salaries (after deducting special, additional special, and other legally determined items) obtained by taxpayers does not exceed $5000$ yuan (commonly known as the "threshold") is not taxable, and the part exceeding $5000$ yuan is the taxable income for the whole month. The new tax rate table is as follows:

2019年1月1日后个人所得税税率表

| 全月应纳税所得额 | 税率$(\%)$ |
|------------------|------------|
| 不超过$3000$元的部分 | $3$ |
| 超过$3000$元至$12000$元的部分 | $10$ |
| 超过$12000$元至$25000$元的部分 | $20$ |
| 超过$25000$元至$35000$元的部分 | $25$ |

Individual income tax special additional deductions refer to the six special additional deductions specified in the individual income tax law, including child education, continuing education, serious illness medical treatment, housing loan interest, housing rent, and supporting the elderly. Among them, supporting the elderly refers to the support expenses for parents and other legally supported persons aged $60$ and above paid by taxpayers. It can be deducted at the following standards: for taxpayers who are only children, a standard deduction of $2000$ yuan per month is allowed; for taxpayers with siblings, the deduction amount of $2000$ yuan per month is shared among them, and the amount shared by each person cannot exceed $1000$ yuan per month.

A taxpayer has only one older sister, and both of them meet the conditions for supporting the elderly as specified. If the taxpayer's personal income tax payable in May 2020 is $180$ yuan, then the taxpayer's monthly salary after tax in that month is ____ yuan.

During the month of May, Andrew purchases cookies from two different bakeries. From Monday to Friday, he buys 4 cookies per day. Two of these cookies cost 15 dollars each while the other two cost 18 dollars each. On weekends, he buys 5 cookies per day, with three of them costing 12 dollars each and the other two costing 20 dollars each. How much did Andrew spend on cookies in May, considering there are 22 weekdays and 9 weekend days?

To get to school, Jenny decided to ride the school's double decker bus. The bus has a total of 25 rows of seats, with 15 rows on the lower deck and 10 rows on the upper deck. On the lower deck, each row has a capacity of 5 kids, while on the upper deck, each row can seat up to 3 kids. Additionally, 4 staff members must also ride the bus. How many kids can ride the school bus in total, considering staff members occupy available seats?

The school nurse must conduct lice checks at the elementary school. She must check 26 Kindergarteners, 19 first graders, 20 second graders, 25 third graders, 30 fourth graders, and 28 fifth graders. Additionally, she must complete a two-minute vision test and a three-minute hearing test for each student, along with the two-minute lice check. How many hours will it take the nurse to complete all the checks and tests for all students?

Pete must finish paying off the last $90 he owes on a bike. He goes through his wallet and finds two $20 bills. Checking his pockets, he finds some $10 bills. Unhappy that he doesn't have the entire amount, he suddenly remembers that he has plastic bottles that can be returned to his local store for cash. If the store pays 50 cents for each bottle and Pete needs to return 20 bottles, how many $10 bills does Pete have in his pockets?

Mimi has decided to start going to the gym again. Over the weekend, she spent $12,000 on athletic sneakers and clothes. She spent twice as much on Nike sneakers as she did on Adidas. What she spent on Adidas was 1/3 the cost of Skechers, and she also bought Puma sneakers worth 3/4 of the cost of Nike sneakers. Mimi's Adidas purchase was $900 before a 10% discount. After considering the discount, what amount did she spend on clothes?

Janna sleeps 7 hours each day from Monday to Wednesday, and 8 hours each day on the weekends. However, on Thursdays due to her work schedule she only manages to sleep 6 hours, and on Fridays due to exhaustion she sleeps 9 hours. She also has a habit of taking a 20-minute nap after lunch on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and a 45-minute nap on Saturdays. Considering all her sleep and naps, how many hours does she sleep in a week?

Mary is going on a business trip. It takes some time for her Uber to get to her house and 5 times longer to get to the airport. It takes 15 minutes to check her bag and three times as long to get through security. Then she has to wait for 20 minutes for her flight to start boarding and twice as long before the plane is ready to take off. This process will take 3 hours total. How long does it take for her Uber to get to her house?

Jennifer wants to go to two museums and a cultural center. The first museum is 5 miles away from her home, the second museum is 15 miles away, and the cultural center is 10 miles away. Due to a sudden traffic detour, Jennifer has to take an extra 3 miles on her way to the first museum. If Jennifer goes to each location on separate days, how many miles total will she travel, considering the detour on her way to the first museum?

John is a door-to-door salesman. He visits 50 houses a day, and on average, 30% of the customers buy something from him. Out of those customers:

- 35% buy a $50 set of knives,
- 40% buy a $150 set of knives,
- 15% buy a $75 kitchen gadget, and
- 10% buy a $200 deluxe kitchen set.

How much does he sell in a week when he works 6 days a week, considering that on the last day of the week, he offers a 10% discount on all products?

Andrew purchased 7 kg of grapes at the rate of $68 per kg, 9kg of mangoes at the rate of $48 per kg, 5 kg of apples at the rate of $55 per kg, and 4 kg of oranges at the rate of $38 per kg. The shopkeeper offers a 10% discount on the total cost of grapes and mangoes, and there is a 5% sales tax applied to the total cost of all fruits purchased. How much amount did he pay to the shopkeeper after considering discounts and taxes?

An industrial vehicle typically requires maintenance checks every 50 days. However, with the application of three different protective additives, the time between required maintenance checks is increased. Additive A increases the maintenance interval by 20%, additive B by 30%, and additive C by 40%. If all three additives are used simultaneously, what is the combined percentage increase in the time between maintenance checks?

An industrial vehicle requires maintenance checks every 45 days. The owner decides to use two different protective additives to extend the time between maintenance checks. Additive A increases the time between maintenance checks by 35%, and Additive B increases the time by 20% of the remaining time after using Additive A. Calculate the total percentage increase in time between maintenance checks when both additives are used.

Janet is getting paid to moderate social media posts. She gets paid 25 cents for each text post, 30 cents for each image post, and 40 cents for each video post she checks. The time it takes her to check a post varies based on the type: 10 seconds for text posts, 20 seconds for image posts, and 1 minute for video posts. In an hour, she checks 150 text posts, 80 image posts, and 20 video posts. How much does she earn per hour?

A car during its journey travels 1 hour at a speed of 40 kmph and experiences an elevation gain of 500 meters, then drives for 30 minutes at a speed of 60 kmph with a consistent headwind that decreases speed by 5 kmph, and finally 2 hours at a speed of 60 kmph with an elevation loss of 1000 meters. Considering the effects of elevation change and wind resistance, calculate the average speed of the car throughout the journey.

Samuel joined coaching on New Year's Day and took coaching every day without fail until he discontinued on November 4. The coaching charges are 23 dollars per day. However, Samuel received a 10% discount on the fees for every 30 consecutive days of coaching, and there were 5 public holidays during which coaching did not take place. Considering the year is not a leap year, calculate the total coaching fee Samuel has to pay.

A driver consumes a certain amount of alcohol, causing the alcohol content in their blood to rise to 1mg/mL. If after stopping drinking, the alcohol content in their blood decreases at a rate of 20% per hour, how many hours will it take for the alcohol content to decrease to 20mg in 100mL of blood, which is the threshold for being considered safe to drive under the influence? Express your answer as a whole number of hours.

Jonathan wants to buy a dictionary that costs $11, a dinosaur book that costs $19, a children's cookbook that costs $7, an atlas that costs $15, and a set of picture books costing $32. He finds a coupon that offers a 5% discount on his total purchase before taxes. The tax rate is 8%. He has already saved $8 from his allowance. How much more money does Jonathan need to buy all five books, considering the discount and tax?

You enter a weight loss challenge game with a goal to lose 15% of your body weight. During the challenge, you manage to lose 12% of your body weight. However, for the final weigh-in, you are required to wear clothes that add 3% to your weight and drink a beverage of 500 ml which weighs 0.5% of your starting weight. Considering the additional variables, what is the measured percentage of weight loss at the final weigh-in?

Jacque arrived in France and his suitcase weighed some pounds. While in France, he picked up 5 bottles of perfume that weighed 1.2 ounces each, 4 pounds of chocolate, 2 bars of soap that weighed 5 ounces each, and 2 jars of jam that weighed 8 ounces each. Considering 16 ounces is the same as 1 pound, Jacque's suitcase weighed 11 pounds on the return flight home. How much did his suitcase weigh when he arrived in France?

Janet is considering three options to retile her bathroom. The turquoise tiles cost $13/tile, the purple tiles cost $11/tile, and the orange tiles cost $15/tile. If Janet needs to tile three walls that measure 5 feet by 8 feet, 7 feet by 8 feet, and 6 feet by 9 feet, and each square foot of wall takes 4 tiles, how much will Janet save by buying the least expensive tiles instead of the most expensive ones for each wall?

A bus has three types of stoppages: short, medium, and long. Excluding stoppages, the speed of the bus is 90 km/hr, and including all stoppages, it is 84 km/hr. If the bus has 2 short stoppages in an hour, each lasting 30 seconds, 1 medium stoppage lasting 3 minutes, and 1 long stoppage every 2 hours lasting 5 minutes, how many minutes does the bus stop per hour on average, considering all types of stoppages combined?

Jerry needs to purchase a black-and-white cartridge and three color cartridges to get his printer to work. The black-and-white cartridge costs $27, with a 10% discount, while each color cartridge costs $32, with a 5% discount. Additionally, Jerry must pay a 7% sales tax on the total cost after applying the discounts. Calculate the total cost Jerry has to pay, considering the different discount rates and the sales tax.

If the first skyscraper was built 100 years ago and the tallest skyscraper today is 3 times taller than the first one, how many years in the future will it be until it takes twice the time to climb the first skyscraper's height to reach the top of a skyscraper that is built and designed to be 25% taller than the currently tallest skyscraper, considering that it takes 1 hour to climb the height of the first skyscraper?

Jacque arrived in France and his suitcase weighed 5 pounds. While in France, he picked up 5 bottles of perfume that weighed 1.2 ounces each, 4 pounds of chocolate, some bars of soap that weighed a certain amount of ounces each, and 2 jars of jam that weighed 8 ounces each. Considering 16 ounces is the same as 1 pound, Jacque's suitcase weighed 11 pounds on the return flight home. How much did each bar of soap weigh?

A towel can be folded at most p times in total due to its material constraint. Before being bleached, it can be folded optimally n times lengthwise and m times widthwise such that n + m ≤ p. After bleaching, the towel loses 20% of its length and 10% of its breadth. Calculate the maximum percentage decrease in area after unfolding, considering the compounding effects of folding, bleaching, and the folding constraint.

On a shopping trip in a crowded store, Josie had to wait 3 minutes for a cart, some minutes for an employee to unlock a cabinet to get her a product, 14 minutes for a stocker to restock a shelf with what she wanted, and 18 minutes in line to check out. Her shopping trip took an hour and a half, and she spent 42 minutes shopping instead of waiting. How many minutes did Josie wait for an employee to unlock a cabinet?

Oceanside Bike Rental Shop charges a base fee of 17 dollars plus 7 dollars an hour for renting a standard bike. Additionally, they offer optional add-ons such as a helmet for a flat fee of 5 dollars, and a bike lock for an hourly fee of 2 dollars. Tom paid a total of 95 dollars to rent a bike, which included the helmet and lock fees. How many hours did he pay to have the bike and additional accessories checked out?

A part-time employee whose hourly wage was decreased by 20 percent and has a varying commission percentage C on their total sales, decided to increase the number of hours worked per week so that the employee's total income (including commissions) did not change. By what percent E should the number of hours worked be increased to maintain the employee's previous income level, considering the commission percentage C?

Jacque arrived in France and his suitcase weighed 5 pounds. While in France, he picked up 5 bottles of perfume that weighed 1.2 ounces each, 4 pounds of chocolate, 2 bars of soap that weighed 5 ounces each, and some jars of jam that weighed a certain amount of ounces each. Considering 16 ounces is the same as 1 pound, Jacque's suitcase weighed 11 pounds on the return flight home. How much did each jar of jam weigh?

Mary is going on a business trip. It takes 10 minutes for her Uber to get to her house and 5 times longer to get to the airport. It takes some time to check her bag and three times as long to get through security. Then she has to wait for 20 minutes for her flight to start boarding and twice as long before the plane is ready to take off. This process will take 3 hours total. How long does it take to check her bag?

Of the 3,500 inhabitants of a town, 60% are adult males, 35% are adult females, and the remaining 5% are children. Among adult males, 55% are literate, while 80% of adult females are literate. The child population is divided into male and female children equally, and their literacy rate is 95%. Considering both the adult and child populations, what percent of the total female inhabitants in the town are literate?

Tomorrow, Pete must finish paying off the last $90 he owes on a bike. He goes through his wallet and finds two $20 bills. Checking his pockets, he finds four $10 bills. Unhappy that he doesn't have the entire amount, he suddenly remembers that he has plastic bottles that can be returned to his local store for cash. If the store pays 50 cents for each bottle, how many bottles will Pete have to return to the store?

On a shopping trip in a crowded store, Josie had to wait 3 minutes for a cart, 13 minutes for an employee to unlock a cabinet to get her a product, some minutes for a stocker to restock a shelf with what she wanted, and 18 minutes in line to check out. Her shopping trip took an hour and a half, and she spent 42 minutes shopping instead of waiting. How many minutes did Josie wait for a stocker to restock a shelf?

On her baking spree, Laura made 53 lemon cupcakes and 76 chocolate cupcakes which were meant to be given to an orphanage. However, she accidentally left 7 lemon cupcakes and 8 chocolate cupcakes at home. Each box can only hold 5 cupcakes, either of the same type or mixed. How many boxes did Laura end up delivering to the orphanage? Note that some cupcakes might be left out if they don't fill up a box completely.

A school is adding 20 rows of seats to the auditorium. Each row has 15 seats and each seat costs $50. A parent, being a seat manufacturer, offers a tiered discount: 10% discount on each group of 10 seats purchased, 15% discount on each group of 20 seats purchased, and 20% discount on each group of 30 seats purchased or more. How much will the school pay for the new seats considering this tiered discount system?

Emma has saved $1,200 in her bank account. On Monday, she withdrew 8% of her balance to buy a new pair of shoes. The next day, she deposited 25% of the amount she withdrew on Monday. On Wednesday, Emma received her paycheck and deposited 150% of the amount she spent on shoes. One week later, she withdrew 5% of her current balance to contribute to a friend's birthday gift. How much is in her bank account now?

Assuming both the "progress rate" and "regress rate" are 1%, we can consider (1+1%)^365 as the "progress value" after 365 days, and (1-1%)^365 as the "regress value" after 365 days. Calculate the ratio of the "progress value" to the "regress value" after 300 days, using the reference data: lg 101≈2.0043, lg 99≈1.9956, 10^0.87≈7.41. Express your answer as a single number, rounded to the nearest whole number.

Jacque arrived in France and his suitcase weighed 5 pounds. While in France, he picked up 5 bottles of perfume that weighed 1.2 ounces each, some pounds of chocolate, 2 bars of soap that weighed 5 ounces each, and 2 jars of jam that weighed 8 ounces each. Considering 16 ounces is the same as 1 pound, Jacque's suitcase weighed 11 pounds on the return flight home. How many pounds of chocolate did he pick up?

Kaiden and Adriel were to pick a certain number of apples from their farm. After picking 400 apples each, they realized they still had to pick some more, so each picked 3/4 times as many as they had picked earlier. When they checked the pickup truck that was carrying the apples, they found out they still needed to pick 600 apples each to reach the target number. How many apples were they targeting to pick?

To understand the scores of the senior high school mathematics mock examination in School A, B, and C in a certain city, a stratified sampling method is used. The samples are taken from 1260 exam papers in School A, 720 exam papers in School B, and 900 exam papers in School C. If 45 exam papers were drawn from the 900 exam papers of School C, how many exam papers were checked in total during this survey?

A hurricane is approaching the southern coast of Texas, and a rancher is planning to move some head of cattle 60 miles to higher ground to protect them from possible inland flooding that might occur. His animal transport truck holds 20 head of cattle. Traveling at 60 miles per hour, it took him 40 hours to transport all of his cattle to higher ground. How many head of cattle did the rancher have to move?

Given that the initial cost of a car is 150,000 yuan, and the annual expenses for insurance, tolls, and gasoline are about 15,000 yuan, and considering that the maintenance cost for the first year is 3,000 yuan and increases by 3,000 yuan each year thereafter, calculate the optimal year to scrap the car based on the lowest average annual cost. Express your answer as a whole number representing the year.

Dexter went to the mall and saw that Apple products are on sale. He wants to buy an iPhone 12 with a 15% discount and an iWatch with a 10% discount. The price tag shows that an iPhone 12 costs $800 while an iWatch costs a certain amount. Upon check out, he will receive a further 2% cashback discount. The items cost in total $931 after the discount and cashback. What is the original price of the iWatch?

Everett worked varying hours each day with an average of 5 hours per weekday and 6 hours on weekends. Additionally, he worked for a total of 140 hours over a certain period and earned $300 in overtime pay during a public holiday. The overtime rate for holiday work is double his normal rate, which is $15 per hour. Considering the overtime and his varying work hours, over how many weeks did Everett work?

Michael buys his suit for $430, shoes for $190, a dress shirt for $80, and a tie for $50. He gets a $100 discount on the suit, a $30 discount on the shoes, and a 20% discount on the dress shirt and tie together. The tax rate for the suit is 5%, for the shoes it's 7%, for the dress shirt it's 6%, and for the tie it's 4%. Calculate the total amount paid to the seller, considering the discounts and taxes.

A baker sells pastries for $5 on weekdays and $6 on weekends. He works 7 days a week. On Monday he sold 2 pastries. Every weekday, the number of sales increases by 2 compared to the previous day, and on weekends the sales increase by 3 compared to the previous day. Considering the cost fluctuations and varying sales increments, calculate the average number of pastries he sells on each day of the week.

During a journey, a bus travels at varying speeds and stops at irregular intervals. When the bus is in motion, its average speed is 75 km/hr, while its overall average speed, including stoppages, is 40 km/hr. Determine the average time in minutes the bus spends stopped per hour, considering the entire journey consisted of both high-speed and low-speed segments, as well as stops of different durations.

Sally and Bob have made plans to go on a trip at the end of the year. They both decide to work as babysitters during the weekdays and save half of what they've earned for their trip. If Sally makes $6 per day and Bob makes $4 per day, how much money will they both have saved for their trip after considering that they do not work on weekends and they take off a total of 10 holidays throughout the year?

If Jade earns $2800 per month and contributes 8% of her income to her 401(k), while her tax deductions amount to 10% of her income, she spends 55% of her post-deduction income on living expenses, 20% on insurance, 12% on transportation, and 8% on utilities. She saves the remaining portion. If her salary is paid bi-weekly, how much does she save per month after considering all deductions and expenses?

Ayen jogs for 30 minutes every day during weekdays. This week on Tuesday, she jogged 5 minutes more and also jogged 25 minutes more on Friday. Additionally, Ayen jogged for 45 minutes on Saturday and went swimming for 1 hour on Sunday. Swimming can be considered to be the equivalent of 1.5 times the duration of jogging in terms of exercising. How many hours, in total, did Ayen jog and swim this week?

A herring has 40 oz of fat, an eel 20 oz, a pike 10 more oz of fat than an eel, a salmon 35 oz, and a halibut has 50 oz. During cooking, each fish loses 10% of its initial fat content, and 8% of the remaining fat is considered indigestible. If Ellianna cooked and served 40 herrings, 30 eels, 25 pikes, 20 salmons, and 15 halibuts, calculate how many ounces of fat were actually ingested by the guests.

A car travels a distance of 624 km in 3 hours. During the first hour, the car travels at a speed of 180 km/h. In the second hour, the car faces wind resistance and its average speed reduces to 160 km/h while going uphill. Finally, during the third hour, the car goes downhill and its speed increases to 220 km/h. Considering these varying speeds and factors, find the total distance covered by the car.

A hurricane is approaching the southern coast of Texas, and a rancher is planning to move 400 head of cattle 60 miles to higher ground to protect them from possible inland flooding that might occur. His animal transport truck holds 20 head of cattle. Traveling at a certain speed, it took him 40 hours to transport all of his cattle to higher ground. What was the speed of the truck in miles per hour?

If 20 men can build a water fountain 56 metres long in 7 days, and they also need to construct a surrounding stone wall that takes an additional 3 days to build, what total length of a similar water fountain with its surrounding wall can be built by 35 men in 9 days, considering that they will be constructing the wall using a more time-efficient material that reduces wall construction time by 50%?

Sean buys 4 cans of soda, 3 soups, 2 sandwiches, and 1 salad. Each soup costs as much as the 2 combined sodas, and the sandwich costs 4 times as much as the soup. The salad costs twice the price of the sandwich. Sean also has a 10% discount coupon, but he needs to pay a 5% sales tax on the total amount. If each soda costs $1, how much did everything cost together, considering the discount and tax?

Gopi initially gives his servant a salary of Rs. 90 plus one turban for one year. However, after every 3 months, the servant receives a 5% raise in his cash salary based on his initial salary. The servant then leaves after completing a total of 9 months of service and receives Rs. 80 and the turban as his payment. Find the price of the turban, considering the raise in salary after every 3 months.

Pete must finish paying off the last $90 he owes on a bike. He goes through his wallet and finds two $20 bills. Checking his pockets, he finds four $10 bills. Unhappy that he doesn't have the entire amount, he suddenly remembers that he has plastic bottles that can be returned to his local store for cash. Pete needs to return 20 bottles to the store. How much does the store pay for each bottle?

Consider four individuals, A, B, C, and D, whose salaries together amount to $4000. A spends 95% of their salary, B spends 85% of their salary, C spends 80% of their salary, and D spends 75% of their salary. If the sum of A's and B's savings is equal to C's savings, and D's savings are twice B's savings, what are the salaries of A, B, C, and D, given that B's salary is three times C's salary?

Genevieve picked some cherries from the supermarket shelves that cost $8 per kilogram. The supermarket had an offer of a 10% discount on the price of cherries. When Genevieve reached the checkout counter and the discount was applied, she realized she was $400 short of the total price, and her friend Clarice chipped in. If Genevieve had $1600 on her, how many kilograms of cherries did she buy?

Two fast typists can type a document in 2 hours, while three slow typists can type the same document in 3 hours. Let \( a = \sin 1^\circ \cdot \sin 2^\circ \cdot \sin 3^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 89^\circ \) and \( b = \sin 1^\circ \cdot \sin 3^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 87^\circ \cdot \sin 89^\circ \). Then, \( \frac{a}{b} = \sin 2^\circ \cdot \sin 4^\circ \cdot \sin 6^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 88^\circ \).

Applying the double angle formula, we find:

\[ 
\frac{a}{b} = 2^{44} \cdot \sin 1^\circ \cdot \sin 2^\circ \cdot \sin 3^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 44^\circ \cdot \cos 1^\circ \cdot \cos 2^\circ \cdot \cos 3^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \cos 44^\circ
\]

From which it follows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
& b = \sin 1^\circ \cdot \sin 3^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 87^\circ \cdot \sin 89^\circ = \\
& = \frac{a}{2^{44} \cdot \sin 1^\circ \cdot \cos 1^\circ \cdot \sin 2^\circ \cdot \cos 2^\circ \ldots \cdot \sin 44^\circ \cdot \cos 44^\circ} = \\
& = \frac{\sin 1^\circ \cdot \sin 2^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 89^\circ}{2^{44} \cdot \sin 1^\circ \cdot \cos 1^\circ \cdot \sin 2^\circ \cdot \cos 2^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 44^\circ \cdot \cos 44^\circ} = \\
& = \frac{\sin 45^\circ \cdot \sin 46^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 89^\circ}{2^{44} \cdot \cos 1^\circ \cdot \cos 2^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \cos 44^\circ} = \\
& = \frac{\sin 45^\circ \cdot \sin 46^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 89^\circ}{2^{44} \cdot \sin 89^\circ \cdot \sin 88^\circ \cdot \ldots \cdot \sin 46^\circ} = \frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{2^{44}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2^{45}}
\end{aligned}
\]

Let $m$ be the number of coins in the treasure. By morning, the number of remaining coins $N$ is given by

$$
\begin{gathered}
N = \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{2}{3}(m-1) - 1\right) - 1\right) = \frac{2^3}{3^3}(m-1) - \frac{2}{3} - \frac{2^2}{3^2} \\
N = \frac{2^3}{3^3}(m-1) - \frac{10}{9} = 3n \\
8(m-1) - 30 = 81k, \text{ hence }\left\{\begin{array}{c}
m-1 = 3t, \\
8t - 27k = 10
\end{array}\right., \left\{\begin{array}{c}
m = 3t + 1 \\
k = 2s \\
4t - 27s = 5
\end{array}\right.
\right.
\left\{\begin{array}{c}
m = 3t + 1 \\
k = 2s, \\
t = 8 + 27u, \\
s = 1 + 4u
\end{array}\right.
\end{gathered}
$$

Given the constraints

$$
\begin{gathered}
110 \leq 81u + 25 \leq 200, \text{ thus } u=2, m=187. \\
m_1 = 1 + \frac{187 - 1}{3} = 63, \quad \widetilde{m}_1 = 63 + 18 = 81 \\
- \text{ coins of the first pirate; } \\
m_2 = 1 + \frac{187 - 63 - 1}{3} = 42, \quad \widetilde{m}_2 = 42 + 18 = 60 \\
m_3 = 1 + \frac{187 - 63 - 42 - 1}{3} = 28, \quad \widetilde{m}_3 = 28 + 18 = 46 \\
- \text{ coins of the third pirate; } \\
m_0 = \frac{187 - 63 - 42 - 28}{3} = 18 \\
\text{- coins each receives in the morning. }
\end{gathered}
$$
answer: first pirate 81 coins, second pirate 60 coins, third pirate 46 coins

The next day, due to the warm and sunny weather, she found it easier to pull weeds, and her efficiency increased by 50%. However, because of the time constraint, she ended up pulling three times the number of weeds she did the day before. On Thursday, her allergies bothered her and she wore a mask that made it difficult to breathe, reducing her efficiency to one-fifth of what it was on Tuesday. Finally, on Friday it rained for half the day, making it difficult for Sarah to pull weeds, so her efficiency was only 75% of her work on Tuesday, and she managed to pull up 10 fewer weeds than she did on Thursday. Taking into account the weather conditions, her allergies, and the 4-hour daily time constraint, how many weeds did she pull up in total?

Gilbert is an enthusiastic gardener who loves growing herbs in his yard to use in his cooking. At the beginning of the spring, he planted eight different types of herbs: three basil bushes, one parsley plant, two types of mint, one rosemary plant, and one thyme plant. Each herb has a different growth rate: basil doubles every two weeks, parsley grows steadily with one new plant each week, mint triples each month, rosemary and thyme stay the same.

Halfway through spring, which was six weeks long, one of the basil plants bloomed flowers and dropped seeds, resulting in an extra basil plant in his garden. Unfortunately, during the same week, weather damage ruined all the mint plants, so they didn't grow any further for the rest of the season. Also, in the fifth week, an infestation of caterpillars devoured two of the parsley plants. By the time spring ended, how many herb plants did Gilbert have in his garden?

Two woodcutters, Ivan and Prokhor, were working in the forest and sat down for a snack. Ivan had 4 loaves, and Prokhor had 8. A hunter approached them.

"Brothers, I've lost my way in the forest, it's far to the village, and I'm very hungry. Please share your bread with me!"

"Well, sit down, and we'll share what we've got," said the woodcutters.

The twelve loaves were divided equally among the three of them. After eating, the hunter rummaged through his pockets, found a 10-kopeck and a 50-kopeck coin, and said:

"Sorry, brothers, I have nothing more. Share this as you see fit."

The hunter left, and the woodcutters argued. Prokhor said: "I think the money should be divided equally!" But Ivan protested: "For 12 loaves - 60 kopecks, so for each loaf 5 kopecks. Since you had 8 loaves, you get 40 kopecks, and I had 4 loaves, so I get 20 kopecks!" How would you divide this money between the woodcutters?

A hated C and decided to kill him by poisoning his drinking water (the only water supply C had). Independently, another caravaner B also decided to kill C and, not knowing that the water had already been poisoned by A, made a small hole in the water container so that the water would slowly leak out. A few days later, C died of thirst. The question is, who is the killer? A or B?

Some people argue that B is the killer because C never had a chance to drink the poisoned water and would have died even if A had not poisoned it. Others argue that A is the killer because B's actions did not affect the outcome; since A poisoned the water, C was doomed and would have died even if B had not made the hole in the water container.

Whose reasoning is correct?

top row of blocks to the bottom results in a grid with a different numbering but the same
coloring as Grid A.
What is the probability that Sophia receives a citrus grid of blocks?

Let $C$ be the point on the highway where Kolya got off his bike, with $AC=10t$ and $D$ be the point where Vasya was at time $t$, with $AD=5t$. Let $E$ be the point where Petya picked up Vasya on the bike.

On the segment $DC$, with length $|DC|=10t-5t=5t$, Vasya and Petya approached each other at a speed of 20 km/h, and they met at point $E$ at time $t + \frac{10t - 5t}{20} = \frac{5t}{4}$.

Given that $DE = 5 \cdot \frac{t}{4}$, $EC = 15 \cdot \frac{t}{4}$, $CB = 20 - 10t$, and $BE = \frac{15t}{4} + 20 - 10t = 20 - \frac{25t}{4}$,

Vasya and Petya's trip end time is $T_{1} = t + \frac{t}{4} + \frac{20 - \frac{25t}{4}}{10} = 2 + \frac{5t}{8}$.

Kolya's trip end time is $T_{2} = t + \frac{20 - 10t}{5} = 4 - t$

Thus, $T = T(t) = \max\left(T_{1}, T_{2}\right) = \begin{cases}
T_{1} = 2 + \frac{5t}{8}, & t \geq \frac{16}{13} \\
T_{2} = 4 - t, & 0 \leq t < \frac{16}{13}
\end{cases}$

Given that \(\sin 3x \neq 0\) and \(x \neq \frac{\pi k}{3}\):

$$
\begin{gathered}
\sin^2 2x = \cos^2 x + \frac{\cos 3x}{\sin 3x} \\
4 \sin^2 x \cos^2 x - \cos^2 x = \frac{\cos (2x + x)}{\sin 3x} \\
\cos^2 x \left(4 \sin^2 x - 1\right) = \frac{\cos 2x \cos x - \sin 2x \sin x}{\sin 3x} = \frac{\cos^2 x \left(\cos 2x - 2 \sin^2 x\right)}{\sin 3x} \\
= \frac{\cos x \left(1 - 4 \sin^2 x\right)}{\sin 3x}
\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore, the conditions are:
\[
\left\{\begin{array}{c}
\cos x = 0 \\
1 - 4 \sin^2 x = 0
\end{array}\right. 
\]
or \(\sin 3x \cos x = -1\).

The solutions are: 
\[
x = \frac{\pi}{2} + \pi n, \quad x = \pm \frac{\pi}{6} + \pi k.
\]

Moreover:
\[
\left\{
\begin{array}{c}
\sin 3x = -1 \\
\cos x = 1
\end{array}
\right. 
\text { or } 
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
\sin 3x = 1 \\
\cos x = -1
\end{array}
\right.
\]

These systems have no solutions.

How many airplanes? (From the 11th grade, 8 points)

The Absent-minded Scientist's work involves long business trips, and therefore he often flies with the same airline. This airline has many identical airplanes, and they all have names. Since the Scientist does not fly every day and not even every week, it can be assumed that each time he is assigned a random airplane. Out of curiosity and out of habit, every time, the Absent-minded Scientist records the name of the airplane he flies on. On his fifteenth flight, the Scientist found himself on board an airplane proudly named "Siméon Denis Poisson." After takeoff, the Scientist pulled out his booklet to record the airplane's name and discovered that he had already flown on "Poisson" once before, and previously there had been no repetitions. Estimate the number of airplanes in the airline.

Tom, an avid stamp collector, has 3,000 stamps in his collection. He is very sad because he lost his job last Friday. His brother, Mike, and best friend, Harry, try to cheer him up with more stamps, and another friend, Sarah, also decides to join in. However, they want to give the stamps in timed intervals to make the joy last longer. Harry’s gift arrives two days after Mike's gift, and it includes 10 more stamps than twice Mike’s gift. Sarah's gift arrives three days after Harry's gift with 5 fewer stamps than three times the number of stamps Mike gave. Unfortunately, Tom realizes that 37 of his stamps were damaged by water leaks in his storage room. If Mike has given Tom 17 stamps on day one, how many stamps does Tom’s collection now have after receiving gifts from Mike, Harry, and Sarah, and excluding the damaged stamps?

A banker was walking down the street in a small provincial town when he suddenly saw a 5 dollar bill on the pavement. He picked it up, memorized the serial number, and went home for breakfast. During breakfast, his wife told him that the butcher had sent a bill for 5 dollars. Since the banker had no other money on him, he gave the found bill to his wife to pay the bill. The butcher gave this bill to the farmer when he bought a calf, and the farmer gave it to a merchant. The merchant, in turn, gave it to the laundress, who, remembering that she owed the bank 5 dollars, took it there and settled her debt.

The banker recognized the bill, which by that time had been used to pay off debts totaling 25 dollars. Upon closer examination, the bill turned out to be counterfeit. Who lost money and how much in all these transactions?

Draw routes. The diagram shows a simplified map of a certain area. Circles represent towns, and lines represent roads connecting them.

Can you indicate how 5 drivers can travel respectively from \(A\) to \(A\), from \(B\) to \(B\), from \(C\) to \(C\), from \(D\) to \(D\), and from \(E\) to \(E\) without their paths containing any common segments or even intersecting each other?

Draw the required 5 routes; you will likely have to put some thought into it. It does not matter which of the two towns marked with the same letter the route starts or ends in, as the important thing is the roads taken. Note that if you travel from \(A\) to \(A\) vertically down, you will block the route for all other drivers except the one traveling from \(B\) to \(B\), since all drivers must travel only on the roads shown in the diagram.
answer: \text{All paths from $ A \longrightarrow A, B \longrightarrow B, C \longrightarrow C, D \longrightarrow D, E \longrightarrow E$ are non-intersecting and do not share segments.}

problem:
The last time Bob cut his hair, he cut it to 6 inches. Since then, his hair went through three different stages of growth with varying rates and multiple hair cuts in each stage:

Stage 1: Hair grows at a rate of 0.5 inches per month for two years, during which he cuts it twice, each time removing 3 inches.

Stage 2: Hair grows at a rate of 0.7 inches per month for one year and 6 months, during which he cuts it once, removing 5 inches.

Stage 3: Finally, hair grows at a rate of 0.6 inches per month for 'x' years, until it reaches a final length of 36 inches, during which he cuts it once, removing 4 inches.

Calculate the total time (in years and months) it took Bob to grow his hair to 36 inches, taking into account the hair growth rates, cuts, and length removed during each stage.

Arnold's collagen powder has 18 grams of protein for every 2 scoops, so 1 scoop of collagen powder has 9 grams of protein. His protein powder has 21 grams of protein per scoop. And his steak has 56 grams of protein. Additionally, his Greek yogurt has 15 grams of protein per serving, and his almonds contain 6 grams of protein in every 1/4 cup. Since he has a 1/2 cup of almonds, that would be 12 grams of protein.

If he has 1 scoop of collagen powder, 2 scoops of protein powder, his steak, one serving of Greek yogurt, and a 1/2 cup of almonds, how many grams of protein will he consume? To find out, we need to sum up all the protein in these food items:

9 (collagen powder) + 21 * 2 (protein powder) + 56 (steak) + 15 (Greek yogurt) + 12 (almonds) = ? grams of protein consumed

A chocolate box contains 500 bars. Thomas and his 6 friends take 1/3 of the bars and decide to divide them equally between them. However, they notice that one of Thomas's friends, Peter, has a birthday today, so they decide to give him 2 extra bars. Later, Thomas's sister Piper comes home and takes 1/4 of the initial number of chocolate bars to share with her own group of friends, but she decided to give 7 bars back because some of her friends are on a diet. Thomas's other sibling, Paul, who's part of the chess club at school, receives a message from his club members who are craving for some chocolate. He goes ahead and takes 5 more bars than what Piper took minus the bars she returned. How many chocolate bars are left in the box after everyone took their share?

Suppose that Maria Petrovna has \( x \) liters of jam left, and Olga Pavlovna has \( y \) liters of jam left. The values \( x \) and \( y \) are chosen randomly and independently from the interval from 0 to 1. This can be thought of as selecting a random point with coordinates \( (x, y) \) from a unit square \( F \). When Maria Petrovna eats half of her remaining jam, she has \( \frac{x}{2} \) liters left. Therefore, the event \( A \) "Maria Petrovna and Olga Pavlovna have together not less than 1 liter of jam" can be expressed by the inequality \( \frac{x}{2} + y \geq 1 \), which corresponds to the area above the line \( y = 1 - \frac{x}{2} \).

Then the probability of event \( A \) is:

\[
\mathrm{P}(A) = \frac{S_{A}}{S_{F}} = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25
\]

Three students, A, B, and C, participated in the preliminary round of an independent recruitment exam organized by a certain university. The exam results were graded in three levels, with students who received an A grade advancing directly to the second round. It was known from the judges that only one of the three students received an A. The students made predictions about who would advance to the second round as follows: Student A said, "Given C's performance, he can only get a B or C"; Student B said, "I am definitely getting an A"; Student C said, "I really didn't perform well today, I agree with A's prediction." It turned out that only one of these predictions was inaccurate. Therefore, the student who received an A is ______.

Seven dwarfs stood at the corners of their garden, each at one corner, and stretched a rope around the entire garden. Snow White started from Doc and walked along the rope. First, she walked four meters to the east where she met Prof. From there, she continued two meters north before reaching Grumpy. From Grumpy, she walked west and after two meters met Bashful. Continuing three meters north, she reached Happy. She then walked west and after four meters met Sneezy, from where she had three meters south to Sleepy. Finally, she followed the rope by the shortest path back to Doc, thus walking around the entire garden.

How many square meters is the entire garden?

Hint: Draw the shape of the garden, preferably on graph paper.

During a survey about whether high school students have ever smoked, two questions are presented for answering. The inconsequential question is: "Is the last digit of your ID number odd?" The sensitive question is: "Have you ever smoked?" Then, the high school students being surveyed are asked to roll a fair die once, and if an odd number shows up, they answer the first question; otherwise, they answer the second question. Because only the respondents know which question they are answering, they are generally willing to answer truthfully. If this method is applied to 300 surveyed high school students and 80 "Yes" answers are received, then the approximate percentage of people in this group who have smoked is __________.

Jenny and Mark are throwing bottle caps. Jenny's bottle cap flies 18 feet straight, then bounces off a street light and flies another 1/3 of the distance it already went. It then hits a sign and bounces again, flying an additional half of the distance it covered since hitting the street light. 

On the other hand, Mark's bottle cap flies 15 feet forward, then bounces off a window and flies twice as far as it already did. After that, it bounces off a trash can and flies 3/4 of the distance it covered since hitting the window. Finally, it collides with a tree and flies another 30% of the distance it traveled after bouncing off the trash can. 

How much further did Mark's bottle cap go than Jenny's?

At the Boisjoli farm, there is a chicken coop where 270 hens and 3 roosters reside. It is observed that 90% of hens lay an egg every morning, but 40% of them lay at 8 a.m. and the remaining 50% lay at 9 a.m. Ms. Mosel goes to collect the eggs in two rounds, first at 8 a.m. and then at 9 a.m. After each collection, she puts the usable eggs in boxes that can hold 7 eggs each. It takes her 20 minutes to pack the eggs after each collection. On average, 5% of the eggs collected are found broken or unusable and are discarded before boxing. Ms. Mosel repeats this process every day from Monday to Sunday since the chickens don't have a day off. How many boxes of usable eggs does Ms. Mosel fill each week?

Bill decides to bring donuts to work for a meeting that day. He buys a box of donuts that has 50 in total in them. He eats 2 on the ride in because he's hungry. When he gets to the office, the secretary takes another 4 out of the box when he's not looking. Then, his manager grabs 10% of the remaining donuts to share with the other managers. After that, a group of coworkers come by and collectively eat one-third of the donuts left. Lastly, right before the meeting Bill sets the box down on his desk and leaves the office to take a phone call. While Bill's away, his coworkers steal half the remaining donuts. Bill comes back and brings the box into his meeting. How many donuts are left in the box?

In a certain country, there are only liars and economists (liars always lie, and economists always tell the truth). At a certain moment, the country planned to conduct monetary and fiscal reforms. Since it was unknown what the residents actually expected, they were asked several questions with only "yes" or "no" answers. The questions received affirmative answers as follows:

"Will taxes be raised?" $40\%$,

"Will money supply be increased?" $30\%$,

"Will bonds be issued?" $50\%$,

"Will gold and foreign exchange reserves be spent?" $0\%$.

What percentage of the population actually expects the raising of taxes, given that each of them realistically expects only one measure? (14 points)

The heat engine "Lomonosov" 12341 receives heat in segment $1-2$ and gives it off in segment $3-4$. Therefore,

$$
\eta_{0}=1-\frac{Q_{34}}{Q_{12}}
$$

The engine "Avogadro" 1231 receives heat in segment $1-2$ and gives it off in segment $3-1$. Therefore,

$$
\eta_{1}=1-\frac{Q_{13}}{Q_{12}}
$$

The engine "Boltzmann" 1341 receives heat in segment $1-3$ and gives it off in segment $3-4$. Therefore,

$$
\eta_{2}=1-\frac{Q_{34}}{Q_{13}}
$$

By combining the three formulas above, we get

$$
\eta_{2}=\frac{\eta_{0}-\eta_{1}}{1-\eta_{1}}
$$

Given that $\eta_{1}<\eta_{0}$ and $\eta_{2}<\eta_{0}$ for all $\eta_{0}, \eta_{1}<1$, and that $\eta_{1}=(1-0.01 \alpha) \eta_{0}$, find the answer.

Rupert and Ronald aced their math test, so their mother bought them a fantastic trampoline. Over the course of a week, they jumped on the trampoline every day with varying amounts of enthusiasm. On Monday, Ronald jumped 157 times while Rupert jumped 86 more times than Ronald. On Tuesday, Ronald increased his jumps to 193 times while Rupert decreased his jumps by 35 times compared to Monday. On Wednesday, both brothers doubled the number of jumps from their respective Tuesday jumps. For the remaining four days, from Thursday to Sunday, their jumps decreased by a constant rate of 20 times each day. Calculate the total number of jumps made by Rupert and Ronald throughout the week.

Some large numerical problems can be solved by converting them into algebraic expression problems using letters. Please read the following solution process first, and then answer the following question. For example, if $x=6789\times 6786$, $y=6788\times 6787$, compare the sizes of $x$ and $y$. Solution: Let $6788=a$, then $x=\left(a+1\right)\left(a-2\right)=a^{2}-a-2$, $y=a\left(a-1\right)=a^{2}-a$. Since $x-y=(a^{2}-a-2)-(a^{2}-a)=-2$, we have $x < y$. After reading this, have you learned this method? Use the above method to answer the following question: If $x=2007\times 2011-2008\times 2010$, $y=2008\times 2012-2009\times 2011$, compare the sizes of $x$ and $y$.

On Monday, Samson ate 3 sandwiches at lunch and twice as many at dinner. On Tuesday, he ate 4 sandwiches at lunch and half as many at dinner because he felt sick the previous day. However, Samson's appetite increased on Wednesday, so he ate double the number of sandwiches at lunch compared to Tuesday and triple the number for dinner. On Thursday, Samson had a busy day and only had time to eat the same number of sandwiches as other people around him. During lunch, he noticed 3 people around him each ate 2 sandwiches, and at dinner, he mimicked his friend who ate 5 sandwiches. How many more sandwiches in total did Samson eat from Monday to Wednesday than on Thursday?

According to the will of a deceased father, his three sons were to divide 7 horses among themselves so that the eldest would receive half, the middle son a quarter, and the youngest an eighth. The inheritance was very confusing for the heirs since it required cutting the horses into parts. An old neighbor provided a solution: he added his own horse to the 7, making it 8 horses in total. Then the division was straightforward: the eldest received 4 horses (half of 8), the middle son received 2 horses (a quarter of 8), and the youngest received 1 horse (an eighth of 8). Afterward, the neighbor took back his horse. Explain the neighbor’s logic in dividing the horses.
answer: One horse each for eldest and youngest sons, and two horses for the middle son

problem: Marta sells tomatoes in a grocery store. On Friday, a shipment of 1000 kg of tomatoes arrived at the store. On Saturday, Marta sold a total of 300 kg of tomatoes to customers, a selling rate of 60%. On Sunday, the store was closed, and since tomatoes have a spoilage rate of 20% per day, 200 kg of the remaining tomatoes rotted away. On Monday, another shipment arrived, which weighed 1.5 times the first shipment's weight. However, Marta was only able to sell 40% of the total tomatoes available on that day. Additionally, another 15% of the remaining tomatoes spoiled by Tuesday. Calculate the total kilograms of tomatoes Marta had ready for sale on Tuesday.

Isabelle has two siblings, Anna and Alex, and three cousins, Lily, Jack, and Nick she decided to take to a concert. Isabelle gets a 40% employee discount for her own ticket because she works at the concert venue. Her youngest cousin, Nick, as a child, gets a ticket price at 60% of the standard $80 ticket price. The rest of her siblings and cousins are students, therefore they are entitled to a 20% discount on their tickets. Together, they have collectively saved $150 so far. If Isabelle's part-time job pays her $7.50 per week after her essential weekly expenses, how many more weeks does Isabelle need to work to afford the concert tickets for everyone?

Once, in a physics and mathematics school, September was declared the month of information technology. Therefore, every Monday in September there was 1 computer science lesson in each class, every Tuesday - 2 lessons, every Wednesday - 3 lessons, every Thursday - 4 lessons, and every Friday - 5 computer science lessons. Saturdays and Sundays were days off at this school. On September 1, there were ceremonial assemblies at the school, so there were no lessons. It is known that there were a total of 64 computer science lessons in each class throughout September. On which day of the week did September 1 fall that year? September has a total of 30 days.

When Erick went to the market to sell his fruits, he noticed that the price of lemons had risen by 50% and the price of grapes had increased by 25%. In anticipation of these changes, he brought different quantities of each fruit to the market. He had 80 lemons, 140 grapes, 60 oranges, and 100 apples in his basket. He originally planned to sell the lemons at $8 each, grapes at $7 each, oranges at $5 each, and apples at $4 each. However, since the price of oranges increased by 10% and apples by 20%, he needed to update his selling prices.

How much money did he collect from selling the fruits at the new prices if he sold all the fruits in his basket?

Joey the postman has a 5-mile long route to deliver packages in a hilly area. It takes him 2 hours to complete the deliveries with an average speed of 4 miles per hour due to the uphill segments. After delivering all the packages, he returns to the post office along the same path, but at a faster pace since he's going downhill. During his return, the weather turns rainy, causing him to slow down at some sections. If the overall average speed for his round trip is 6 miles per hour, and he spends an extra 15 minutes on the return trip due to the rain, what is his average speed during the downhill return trip excluding the time affected by the rain?

A bus with a capacity of 70 seats is filled with 48 passengers. Two-thirds of them are women and the rest are men. There are 5 children on the bus, who are all seated. Among the men, one-eighth are standing while the rest are seated. 

Three women are unable to sit because they are attending to their prams. If passengers with disabilities must occupy a seat, and knowing that there are 2 passengers with disabilities onboard who are not children or attending to prams, how many men are seated?

Make note, the children could be either boys or girls, and the 3 women attending to the prams are part of the earlier mentioned two-thirds women count.

A man goes into a barbershop and gets a $15 haircut. He pays the barber with a $20 bill, but the barber doesn't have change because it is an especially slow day. The barber goes to the flower shop next to his own and trades the $20 bill for a $10 dollar bill and some other bills. Then he gives the man his change. Later the lady from the flower shop confronts the barber and tells him that the $20 bill he gave her was counterfeit. The barber agrees and he gives the lady a different $20 bill. Later that day he tries to figure out how much money he lost and found out he lost a certain amount. What was the value of the change he gave to the man?

A certain school held a math competition, and students A, B, C, D, and E were the top $5$ winners. Before giving out the awards, the teacher asked them to guess the ranking of each person.
A said: "B is in third place, and C is in fifth place."
B said: "E is in fourth place, and D is in fifth place."
C said: "A is in first place, and E is in fourth place."
D said: "C is in first place, and D is in second place."
E said: "A is in third place, and D is in fourth place."
The teacher said that each ranking was guessed correctly by someone. Therefore, the students who won the first, second, and third places are______.
